summary: Citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival (US$50 plus processing fees) at Dhaka and other international airports, while other nationalities — including Indian citizens — must arrange a visa through a Bangladeshi mission, starting on the official portal visa.gov.bd, before traveling. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Ghana, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.

tips.text: For the visa on arrival, carry the fee (US$50 plus processing fees), your return ticket and hotel details. The UK FCDO says you must have a return ticket and proof of funds, and that officers issue the visa at their discretion.

The UK FCDO warns that political rallies, demonstrations and strikes (hartals) can quickly turn violent, with arson and vandalism in towns and cities. Stay away from protests and large gatherings, and move to a place of safety if one starts.

The Government of Canada says the monsoon runs from June to October and floods a third of the country each year, making roads impassable, and that the coastline is subject to cyclones. Monitor forecasts from the Bangladesh Meteorological Department.

The UK FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the Chittagong Hill Tracts (Rangamati, Khagrachari and Bandarban districts). If you do go, you must give the Bangladeshi authorities 10 days’ notice.

The UK FCDO advises men and women to dress modestly, and women to cover their shoulders and legs in public. During Ramadan, follow local dress codes and check the opening hours of shops and restaurants.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Almost everyone needs one, but many tourists get it at the airport: citizens of the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival for US$50 plus processing fees. Other nationalities apply through a Bangladeshi mission, starting online at visa.gov.bd, where the fee schedule lists the fee for each nationality. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Ghana, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How does Bangladesh's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible travelers pay the fee (US$50 plus processing fees) in US dollars, pounds or euros at Dhaka or another international airport or land port, for a single-entry stay of up to 30 days. Bring a return air ticket, hotel details and at least US$500 in cash or on a credit card — these are conditions of the 2016 circular, and issuance is at the officer's discretion, so confirm eligibility with your airline before flying.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Yes — the UK FCDO says you can apply for a visa extension from the Department of Immigration and Passports. Apply before your current stay expires.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Yes — Indian passport holders are not eligible for the visa on arrival and must obtain a visa in advance from a Bangladeshi mission in India. Apply well before travel, as processing times and requirements change.

faq.question: Is Bangladesh safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Bangladesh, that political demonstrations and strikes can turn violent, and that road accidents are common. It advises against all but essential travel to the Chittagong Hill Tracts. Check your government’s latest advice before you go.
